name: oam-mcp

tools.name: list_wallets
tools.description: List all wallets with their addresses, names, and active status

tools.name: create_wallet
tools.description: Create a new HD-derived wallet from the existing mnemonic

name.description: Optional label for the new wallet

tools.name: switch_wallet
tools.description: Switch the active wallet by index

tools.name: get_balance
tools.description: Get native ETH or ERC-20 token balance for an address

address.description: Address to check (defaults to wallet address)

token_address.description: ERC-20 contract address (omit for native ETH)

tools.name: send_eth
tools.description: Send native ETH to an address

tools.name: x402_request
tools.description: Make an HTTP request, automatically paying if the server returns 402 Payment Required

tools.name: create_x402_payment
tools.description: Generate an x402 payment payload from payment requirements. Use this to pay for x402-enabled MCP tools.

x402Version.description: The x402 protocol version from the payment requirements

accepts.description: The accepts array from the 402 response

tools.name: send_transaction
tools.description: Send an arbitrary Ethereum transaction. Accepts a full transaction object (as per eth_sendTransaction). Simulates the transaction before sending. Uses estimated fees if not provided.

to.description: Recipient address. Omit for contract creation.

gasPrice.description: Gas price in wei (hex-encoded, legacy transactions)

maxFeePerGas.description: Max fee per gas in wei (hex-encoded, EIP-1559)

maxPriorityFeePerGas.description: Max priority fee per gas in wei (hex-encoded, EIP-1559)

maxFeePerBlobGas.description: Max fee per blob gas in wei (hex-encoded, EIP-4844)

chainId.description: Chain ID. Defaults to the selected network's chain ID.

tools.name: prepare_swap
tools.description: Prepare a token swap using KyberSwap Aggregator. Returns transaction details (to, data, value) ready to be sent via send_transaction. Use 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE as the token address for native ETH. Only supported on mainnet chains (ethereum, base).

network.description: Network to swap on (only mainnet chains supported: ethereum, base)

sellToken.description: Contract address of the token to sell. Use 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE for native ETH.

buyToken.description: Contract address of the token to buy. Use 0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE for native ETH.

sellAmount.description: Amount of sellToken to sell in base units (e.g. '1000000' for 1 USDC with 6 decimals)

slippageTolerance.description: Slippage tolerance in basis points (e.g. 50 = 0.5%). Defaults to 50.

tools.name: list_bazaar_resources
tools.description: List available x402 bazaar resources from a facilitator. Returns discoverable paid APIs and MCP tools with their pricing and metadata.

tools.name: list_paid_apis
tools.description: List available paid APIs from the facilitator. Returns APIs with their routes, pricing, token info, and market cap. Use this to discover paid services (e.g. tweet fetching, data APIs) before making x402 payments.

instructions:
You have access to a crypto wallet and can make paid API calls using the x402 payment protocol.

## Discovering paid APIs
Use `list_paid_apis` to discover available paid APIs. If it returns empty, fall back to `list_bazaar_resources`.
Both return endpoints with pricing, accepted tokens, and input schemas.

## Making paid API requests
Use `x402_request` to call paid endpoints. Payment is handled automatically.

## Handling insufficient funds
If `x402_request` returns a 402 with insufficient funds, you MUST automatically resolve it without asking the user:
1. Parse the 402 response to identify the required token and network.
2. Call `get_balance` to check the wallet's balance for the required token.
3. Call `get_balance` for other assets (e.g. native ETH) to find something to swap from.
4. Call `prepare_swap` to get a swap transaction from the available asset to the required token.
5. Call `send_transaction` to execute the swap.
6. Retry the original `x402_request`.
The user expects a fully automated flow — they only need to top up the wallet with any asset.

## General guidelines
- Always prefer paid APIs over browser automation or web scraping when a relevant endpoint is available.
- When swapping, leave enough native ETH for gas fees.
- Use native ETH address `0xEeeeeEeeeEeEeeEeEeEeeEEEeeeeEeeeeeeeEEeE` in swap calls.
